s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic facial swelling and skin lesions with a history of malignancy
salient_findings: Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face
Pain on palpation without fever or chills
Histopathological findings of atypical cells in dilated vessels
key_facts: 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on the face
History of left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier
Treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy
Left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision seven years after initial diagnosis
No fever or chills
Pain on palpation
Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek
Predominantly involving the left side of the face
Histopathological examination showed hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis
Immunohistochemical examination showed epithelial cells in dilated vessels positive for CD31 and atypical cells positive for GATA3

shortlist.label: Postradiation angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of radiation therapy and current presentation of violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showing highly atypical cells in dilated vessels and immunohistochemical examination positive for CD31 and GATA3

shortlist.label: Metastatic breast carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of left breast carcinoma and presence of atypical cells in dilated vessels

shortlist.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of mastectomy and radiation therapy, and current presentation of chronic facial swelling and skin lesions

shortlist.label: Lymphangiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showing dilated vessels in the dermis and immunohistochemical examination positive for CD31

raw.rationale: The patient's history of left breast carcinoma and the presence of atypical cells in dilated vessels positive for GATA3, a marker commonly expressed in breast cancer, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: While the histopathological examination showed dilated vessels with atypical cells, the patient's history of breast carcinoma and the immunohistochemical findings of GATA3 positivity in atypical cells make cutaneous metastasis of breast carcinoma a more likely explanation for the presentation.
